system:
Audit this final H3 composition against its typed responsibilities. Return findings only for clear contradictions, not aesthetic preferences, prose length, optional creative choices, or unknown video quality. The supplied fragments are the actual final narrative, with typed subject/reference IDs printed explicitly. Read their full context and the target subject kinds: a floor or other environment must not become a moving vehicle merely because it is Subject 1. A subject/placed_subject/replacement_subject reference supplies its selected identity properties, not its original background, pose or photographic lighting. An environment reference supplies its scene, not the depicted actor identity or actor-specific appearance. An observed claim copying a mixed source summary must obey the same responsibility: citing the source does not authorize importing all its content. Independently requested or creative content is allowed; a generic car or room resembling a source is not itself evidence of misuse. A source structure/storyboard provides only its declared camera/cutting/planning properties, not its people, objects, world, lighting or palette. A placed subject adds to the edited scene; a replacement takes over the identified source figure. Both must actually appear in prose/actions, not only definitions. Accepted target identity outranks raw source observations. A visual source video does not wire its soundtrack. composition_facts.audio declares the actually wired audio relationships. If its attachments are empty, an explicit claim that the original soundtrack is preserved, reused, played or carried over is audio_signal_misuse even if the task prefix omits reuse. Newly generated sound is permitted and a similar sound does not demonstrate copying. Property-only references preserve their role-specific recipient and do not play the original recording; voice, new-score style, cut/action timing and new sound texture are distinct relationships, never general permission to condition any new sound. BGM music references with partially_copy copy the supplied signal, and prose must not deny that. Music=N/A under no_added_music only prohibits adding a new score; it does not cancel an explicitly copied BGM. References with no actual dialogue do not authorize inventing spoken words. For actual first/last frame responsibilities, the whole supplied still is that frame: reference-sheet panels/labels/background are frame pixels, not packaging to silently remove. Moving one panel within an otherwise preserved sheet is legitimate. A recorded aspect-ratio warning alone is not a contradiction and does not authorize a crop. Do not invent preparation IO or assume its execution. Every finding must identify an actual fragment and an exact nonempty quote from that fragment demonstrating the contradiction, plus the implicated target subject ID when relevant. Empty findings means no clear supported contradiction was found, not proof of overall quality. No Markdown.
Positive replacement obligations: inspect replacement_inheritance and its observed_motion_contexts, not only exclusions. The replacement must inherit the identified source figure's observed motion, position and timing. A global action-governs=request entry authorizes only the actor/action actually requested; changing the car's action does not change the driver's action. Compare the final replacement narrative with the identified figure's motion in context. Standing still is not inheriting an observed crossing action unless the caller explicitly changes that same figure's action. Do not invent timing facts outside the declared coverage.
Finding thresholds: similar sounds are not evidence of copying a recording. Generic newly generated engine ambience, a matching pulse, or an appropriate sound texture is legitimate without an assertion that the source recording is played. For audio_signal_misuse quote an explicit source-signal relationship contradicting the typed copy/property role; never infer copying solely from sonic resemblance. Likewise camera movement after an anchored instant is legitimate. A push-in, pan or other dynamic camera event alone does not demonstrate that the initial or final anchor frame was changed. Report frame_content_changed only when actual narrative asserts incompatible frame content or a crop/removal at that anchored instant. These constraints are mandatory; do not report speculative contradictions.
The typed claims preserve their explicit origins. A user-origin claim records caller authorization or a requested outcome; it is not itself evidence that the final narrative executes that outcome or copies an original signal. User claims are deliberately absent from executable fragment addresses. Compare the actual final narrative, source bindings and typed performance events to that authorization. Observed and creative claims remain auditable executable assertions.

fragments.shot:shot-1:description: The complete first supplied reference sheet fills the frame exactly as supplied at the zero-millisecond anchor: the vertical sheet keeps its rainy nighttime hero panel at the top, its FRONT, SIDE PROFILE and BACK studio turnaround panels in the middle, and its FACE, JACKET COLLAR, HANDS and BOOTS detail panels at the bottom, with every panel and every existing label held in its original position. In the hero panel the adult woman stands upright on a wet, reflective industrial walkway or rooftop, rain falling around her, metal railings and blurred city lights behind her, warm amber light from a building on the right; she has short dark hair with shaved sides and a longer top pulled back, medium-light skin, a visible diagonal scar near one eyebrow, a black collared utility jacket over a dark shirt, black cargo-style trousers and black lace-up combat boots, with her arms at her sides, her head turned toward the viewer's left and a neutral, serious expression. The studio panels show the same person in full-body front, side-profile and rear views plus the face, jacket collar, weathered hands and worn boot details against a dark gray backdrop under dim, soft directional light. The whole sheet remains intact as a slow, even visual dissolve begins around three seconds in, softly starting to reveal the second supplied sheet without cropping, extracting or rearranging any part of the first.
fragments.shot:shot-1:event:0: The camera holds a static shot.
fragments.shot:shot-2:description: The slow visual dissolve continues without hurry from the opening of the shot, carrying the first sheet away and resolving onto the entire second supplied reference sheet exactly as supplied: the volcanic hero panel of the black dragon across the top, and the FRONT, SIDE PROFILE, REAR, HEAD CLOSE, WING MEMBRANE, CLAW AND FOOT and SCALE DETAIL panels in their rows below, every existing caption intact and every panel held in its original layout. In the hero panel the large quadrupedal dragon stands on dark, wet volcanic rock, its body in profile facing left with the head lowered, glossy black plated scales showing subtle blue-teal iridescence, a row of dorsal spikes running along the neck, back and long tail, two long pale ridged horns swept back from the crown, smaller horns and jaw spikes, large dark leathery membranous wings partially spread and folded above the back with visible fingers and tattered trailing edges, and four legs with pale curved talons; beyond it are jagged rock formations, mist and glowing orange lava or embers under low-key cool blue-gray ambient haze. The labeled turnaround and detail panels show the same dragon from the front, side profile and rear, then the narrow amber-yellow eye and pale horns in the head close-up, the wing membrane, the clawed foot with long curved pale talons, and the scale texture against a plain dark gray studio backdrop. By the final frame the second sheet is held complete and unaltered at the eight-second endpoint, with the first sheet fully gone.
fragments.shot:shot-2:event:0: The camera holds a static shot.

card.environment: Nighttime rainy industrial walkway or rooftop with wet reflective pavement, metal railings, and blurred city lights for the hero image; dark gray studio backdrop for the turnaround and detail panels.
card.lighting: Hero image is lit with cool blue ambient night light and warm amber practical lights; studio panels use dim, soft directional lighting with deep shadows.

facts.text: The image is a vertical character reference sheet: a cinematic hero image occupies the top section; below it are three full-body studio panels labeled FRONT, SIDE PROFILE, and BACK, followed by four detail panels labeled FACE, JACKET COLLAR, HANDS, and BOOTS.

The hero panel shows an adult person standing upright on a wet, reflective industrial walkway or rooftop at night, with rain falling, metal railings, blurred city lights, and warm amber light from a building on the right.
The person has short dark hair with shaved sides and a longer top pulled back, medium-light skin, and a visible diagonal scar near one eyebrow.
The person wears a black collared utility jacket over a dark shirt, black cargo-style trousers, and black lace-up combat boots.
In the hero image the person stands with arms at their sides, head turned toward the viewer's left, with a neutral, serious expression.
The middle FRONT panel shows the same person facing the camera in a full-body studio view against a dark gray backdrop.
The SIDE PROFILE panel shows the person in profile facing the viewer's left, and the BACK panel shows the rear view of the jacket, trousers, and boots.
The FACE detail panel is a close crop of the person's face, showing the undercut hairstyle, neutral expression, and scar near the eyebrow.
The JACKET COLLAR detail shows black fabric, a strap, and a metal buckle; the HANDS detail shows weathered hands with visible veins; the BOOTS detail shows worn black leather lace-up combat boots.
The studio panels use dim, soft directional lighting against a dark gray background, while the hero panel uses cool blue night ambience contrasted with warm amber practical lights.

limitations: The hero panel is dark and rainy, obscuring some fine background and clothing texture.
The detail panels are cropped views and do not show the full body or every side of the clothing.

facts.text: The image is a multi-panel character reference sheet for a single dark dragon design, with one large hero panel along the top and seven smaller labeled detail panels arranged in two rows below.
The hero panel shows a large quadrupedal dragon standing on dark, wet volcanic rock, its body in profile facing left with the head lowered.
The dragon is covered in glossy black, heavily plated scales with subtle blue-teal iridescence, and has a row of spikes running along its spine and long tail.
Two long, pale, ridged horns sweep back from the crown of the head, with smaller horns and spikes around the jaw and neck.
The dragon's wings are large, dark and membranous with visible fingers and a tattered, leathery trailing edge, partially spread and folded above the back.
The hero panel background is a dark, hazy volcanic landscape with jagged rock formations, mist, and glowing orange lava or embers near the ground on the right.
Four panels in the middle row show the dragon from the front, side profile prior, and rear, each against a plain dark gray background.
Four detail panels in the bottom row show, left to right, the head close-up, a wing membrane, a clawed foot, and a close-up of the scale texture.
The head close-up panel shows a narrow amber-yellow eye, dark facial scales and the ridged pale horns emerging above the brow.
The claw and foot panel shows thick scaled toes ending in long, curved, pale bone-colored talons.
Visible panel captions read: FRONT, SIDE PROFILE, REAR, HEAD CLOSE, WING MEMBRANE, CLAW AND FOOT, SCALE DETAIL.

limitations: Small panel captions are legible but the very fine scale texture and background details are only partially resolvable at this resolution.
The image is a still reference sheet; no motion, sound or dialogue can be observed.
